name: greenlight
description: greenlight is a refusal-handling skill that lets AI agents autonomously handle model refusals in security-research-type evaluation harnesses. It was created for benchmarking where Claude Code's guardrails trigger exploitation-related refusals, and ships three skill variants: the validated v3 canonical, a richer v5 at a lower evidence bar, and a modular template for building custom skills. The repo includes a detailed validation dossier from paired Opus 4.7 runs, documenting day-level refusal-rate variance (up to 2.6x), prompt-content and placement ablations, retry-recovery mechanisms, and explicit caveats about target-specificity and underpowered sample sizes. It is MIT licensed and intended solely for authorized LLM safety and security research in controlled environments.
highlights: Three skill variants: v3 canonical (validated), v5 (richer, lower evidence bar), and a modular template
Paired validation on Opus 4.7: refusal rate 0.077 vs 0.286 adversarial baseline, pass rate 0.923 vs 0.429 (single-window snapshot)
Documents day-level refusal variance and a paired-comparison methodology with honest null results
Confirmed post-pivot finding: harmless-POC prompt wording cut refusal rate ~8x at p < 0.05 (N=15 paired)
Harness-ready: drops into ~/.claude/skills or any research harness via claude-agent-sdk
curatorNote: Refusal behavior is one of the least documented failure modes of agent eval harnesses, and this repo treats it with real rigor: paired direct comparisons, day-shape variance analysis, and explicit null results. It is rare to see a proof-of-concept publish the methodology lessons alongside the skill itself.
